result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): B states the key idea plainly in a 'Why timing matters' callout. It treats times as approximate, noting that warm or cool kitchens and bigger feeds change the timing and that many starters peak around 4–8 hours. A's diagram is clean, but it puts fixed hour marks on the axis and in the cards ('Peak ≈ hour 6', 'Hour 7 onward') without saying they depend on temperature. It also never spells out why the timing matters as clearly. Both have small label-and-curve overlaps: A's 'dome sinks, gets sour' and B's 'gets sour and weak', plus B's cut-off-looking 'stirred in,' label. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A states the key idea most clearly. The 'Best time to mix' box sits right on the peak, a 'Why timing matters' callout follows, and it frames timing as depending on temperature and feed size ('around 4 to 8 hours'), with a few minor label collisions (a cut-off 'stirred in,' and red text crossing the curve). B is attractive, with jar icons and shaded stage bands, but it puts exact hours on the axis and in each stage card ('Peak ≈ hour 6', 'Hour 7 onward') as if they apply to every kitchen. Its stage labels also don't line up well with their bands ('3 Peak' sits after the peak point), and the 'dome sinks' label crosses the curve.
